page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated virtual server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC 9575F processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The CPU cores operate at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model, providing 12 physical cores with one thread per core. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 10.67 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression tests all placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth for large block reads and writes is strong, ranking in the top 25%. In LLM inference benchmarks, the dual L40S GPUs achieve top-tier text generation speeds of 368.6 tokens per second for small models and strong generation speeds of 35.15 tokens per second for medium models.

The primary tradeoff of this configuration is the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage, which requires external storage solutions. Qualitatively, the server offers high resource density by pairing dual enterprise-grade GPUs with a moderate 12-vCPU allocation, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores but demand substantial VRAM. This server is optimized for AI and machine learning inference, graphics rendering, and single-threaded data processing tasks.
